problem: Modern vision models lack understanding of what representational structure is necessary for compositional generalization—recognizing familiar parts in novel combinations.
approach: The paper formalizes three desiderata (divisibility, transferability, stability) for compositional generalization and derives necessary geometric constraints: representations must decompose linearly into orthogonal per-concept components.
contribution: Shows the Linear Representation Hypothesis is a necessary consequence of compositional generalization, and empirically confirms partial linear factorization with low-rank near-orthogonal factors across CLIP, SigLIP, and DINO.

problem: Language models face a trade-off between parameter efficiency and prediction quality when scaling to improve performance.
approach: ContextLM augments standard pretraining with a next-context prediction objective, building a language model on context embeddings spanning multiple tokens rather than predicting single tokens.
contribution: Demonstrates 39% parameter reduction to achieve baseline perplexity and robust downstream task improvements under equivalent parameter counts across GPT-2 and Pythia backbones.

problem: Structure-augmented retrieval-augmented generation systems suffer from low-quality structures and semantic drift, leading to poor passage retrieval and retrieval suspension.
approach: KG-Translator translates user queries into graph-level clues by leveraging lightweight NER and syntactic parsing to construct a reliable knowledge graph, then uses constrained decoding and ranking for precise passage retrieval.
contribution: Significantly outperforms baselines on five datasets by translating queries to graph clues instead of traditional matching-based paradigms.

problem: Scene graph generation models treat relationships as static unidirectional mappings, violating physical reality and failing to maintain logical consistency when reasoning perspective shifts.
approach: Proposes the Reciprocal Perspective Calibration (RPC) framework which operationalizes the Mutual-Perspective Inverse Relations principle via Adaptive Inverse-Relation Augmentation and Hypernym-Guided Prompts.
contribution: Achieves competitive performance on standard benchmarks while significantly enhancing capability to understand inverse relations, verified by a new inverse consistency evaluation protocol.

problem: Masked diffusion models for language generation depend critically on generation order, and existing methods either hard-code orderings or learn them separately, both incurring extra cost and suboptimal solutions.
approach: Proposes OeMDM to unify various generation orders and MDM, ARM, and block diffusion in a single framework, then introduces LoMDM which jointly learns generation ordering and diffusion backbone from scratch.
contribution: LoMDM outperforms various discrete diffusion models across multiple language modeling benchmarks with learned context-dependent ordering.

problem: Pre-trained vision-language model text embeddings are misaligned with optimal visual prototypes for out-of-distribution detection, creating an intrinsic modality gap.
approach: Proposes an online pseudo-supervised framework that learns class prototypes directly in visual feature space using unlabeled test-time data streams and soft predictions from pre-trained VLMs.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art out-of-distribution detection across various setups by learning visual prototypes from test data with theoretical convergence guarantees.

problem: Existing black-box network generation methods tend to overfit observed data while overlooking network structure and incur substantial computational overhead at scale.
approach: SyNGLER learns low-dimensional latent node embeddings via a latent space network model, then reconstructs the latent space with a distribution-free generator and samples embeddings to produce synthetic networks.
contribution: Provides theoretical guarantees on edge distribution distances while empirically preserving network sparsity and degree heterogeneity with lower computational cost than deep architectures.

problem: Ultra-high-resolution remote sensing imagery leads to quadratic explosion of visual tokens, hindering extraction of small-object information while requiring unpredictable compute.
approach: UHR-BAT uses text-guided multi-scale importance estimation for token selection and region-wise preserve-and-merge strategies to compress visual tokens under strict context budget.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art performance across various benchmarks while efficiently handling query-critical fine details in kilometer-scale imagery.

problem: Traditional visual grounding relies on fixed last hidden layers which sequentially amplify cumulative errors, and uses semantic tokens without explicit spatial cues.
approach: UGround dynamically selects intermediate transformer layers via reinforcement learning, using stochastic skip connections and mask-as-prompt with spatial similarity maps to guide mask generation.
contribution: Unifies visual grounding across attribute perspectives (from refer expression segmentation to new tasks) while reducing cumulative errors through dynamic layer selection and explicit spatial guidance.

problem: Hybrid epidemic forecasting models struggle with data sparsity and non-stationary disease dynamics, often relegating mechanistic priors to auxiliary roles and failing to generalize under distribution shift.
approach: EpiDiff synergizes epidemiological domain knowledge with diffusion models via an uncertainty-aware steering mechanism that quantifies mechanistic posterior uncertainty and dynamically modulates the diffusion process.
contribution: Consistently outperforms state-of-the-art baselines in accuracy and robustness particularly under non-stationary distributions, with transparent visualization of when forecasts rely on mechanistic laws versus data-driven patterns.

problem: The mechanisms for extracting abstract structures from continuous, high-dimensional dynamics while enabling structural reuse across contexts remain poorly understood.
approach: Proposes a brain-inspired hierarchical model combining an inverse model for structural extraction with hippocampal-entorhinal coupling that dissociates relational structures from episodic scenes via velocity-driven path integration.
contribution: Demonstrates structural abstraction on rotation dynamics and enables robust prediction with structural reuse across diverse contexts through brain-inspired self-supervised learning.

problem: Vision-language models and agents suffer from visual hallucinations in embodied tasks due to inability to distinguish task-relevant objects from distractors in complex scenes.
approach: SceneDiver uses coarse-to-fine focus plan generation to construct scene graphs, progressively decompose tasks, and distill deliberate focus ability into lightweight VLA adapters.
contribution: Substantially reduces visual hallucinations for both VLMs and VLAs while preserving computational efficiency on embodied AI benchmarks.

problem: Existing image emotion understanding models are limited to coarse-grained perception or lack comprehensive reasoning about emotional attributes and intensity nuances.
approach: Introduces EEmoDB dataset with 1.2M QA pairs and 36K fine-grained assessment samples, and proposes EEmo-Logic MLLM via instruction fine-tuning and task-customized group relative preference optimization.
contribution: Achieves robust performance in emotion QA and fine-grained assessment on in-domain and cross-domain datasets, advancing machine empathy capabilities.

problem: Existing distribution shift theory is limited to narrow settings and provides non-estimable bounds, leaving a gap between theoretical understanding and practical applications.
approach: Proposes gamma*-concept shifts leveraging entropic optimal transport and derives general error bounds unifying covariate and concept shifts, then develops estimators with concentration guarantees.
contribution: Provides rigorous, general tools for analyzing learning error under distribution shift that apply to broad loss functions and stochastic labeling, with the DataShifts algorithm for practical estimation.

problem: Audio-visual speaker tracking datasets are limited to simple scenes with coarse annotations, biasing evaluation toward static co-occurrence rather than robust spatiotemporal modeling.
approach: Introduces AVTrack, a human-centric audio-visual instance segmentation dataset with challenging conditions including camera motion, occlusions, and position changes, with baseline methods provided.
contribution: Reveals substantial performance degradation of existing methods and establishes AVTrack as a challenging benchmark for robust audio-visual scene understanding in dynamic environments.

problem: Direct optimization of synthetic trajectories as discrete samples under extreme compression breaks physical coherence and produces non-physical artifacts that overfit specific models.
approach: CHESS shifts optimization from discrete samples to continuous-time signal trajectories using low-rank spatial coherence and piecewise Chebyshev polynomial parameterization to enforce physical constraints.
contribution: Achieves compression ratios up to 133× per sample with strong cross-architecture generalization and zero-shot adaptation across sampling resolutions, with theoretical smoothness and stability guarantees.

problem: Current steering vector approaches require careful per-SV selection of steering factors and sacrifice generation quality through full-sequence interventions regardless of factor choice.
approach: Proposes joint training of steering factors and directions eliminating post-hoc selection, and introduces Prompt-Only Steering Vectors (PrOSV) that intervene only on prompt tokens using neural scaling theory principles.
contribution: PrOSV outperforms traditional full-sequence steering vectors on AxBench with better tradeoff between model utility and adversarial robustness through joint training.

problem: Effectively aligning graph flow models with complex human preferences or task-specific objectives remains challenging without principled reinforcement learning frameworks.
approach: Graph-GRPO derives analytical transition probability expressions for flow models enabling fully differentiable rollouts, and introduces refinement strategies with localized node/edge perturbation and regeneration.
contribution: Achieves 95.0% and 97.5% Valid-Unique-Novelty scores on planar and tree datasets with only 50 denoising steps, and state-of-the-art performance on molecular optimization tasks.

problem: Data pricing in non-rivalrous markets fundamentally differs from traditional goods, and existing equilibrium notions don't extend naturally to data marketplaces.
approach: Introduces gamma*-equilibrium for data pricing based on Nash equilibrium, studies complementary (Leontief) and substitutable (linear) utility models, developing novel proof techniques via graph-of-deviations.
contribution: Establishes existence, efficiency, and polynomial-time computation guarantees for Leontief utilities in general markets, while proving linear utilities lack equilibrium even with homogeneous buyers.

problem: Deep forecasting models suffer from attenuated periodic perception and entangled trend-noise representations as network depth increases, with channel-independence disrupting cross-variable consistency.
approach: PESD-TSF introduces Multiplicative Periodic Gating with continuous priors, multi-scale structured encoder with detrended attention, and Cross-Scale Collaborative Attention for inter-variable topology recovery.
contribution: Consistently achieves state-of-the-art performance with particularly strong gains on multivariate forecasting involving complex inter-variable coupling through physics-inspired decomposition.

problem: EEG emotion recognition models remain opaque black boxes lacking semantic grounding between abstract neural features and human-interpretable emotional states.
approach: Reframes EEG explainability as cross-modal generation, introducing Facial Emoji Proxy Modeling that translates EEG signals into identity-anonymized facial emojis using expression-modeling backbone and structured semantic regularizer.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art accuracy on EAV and MMER benchmarks while generating semantically faithful facial animations providing transparent windows into neural emotional evolution.

problem: Bayesian uncertainty quantification for fine-tuning large language models faces scalability constraints or yields poorly calibrated posterior uncertainty under distribution shift.
approach: GPan-LoRA integrates neural network-based sparse Gaussian Process approximations with amortized variational inference to preserve Bayesian semantics while maintaining computational scalability.
contribution: Produces well-calibrated uncertainty under distribution shift that mitigates overconfident failures while preserving competitive task performance through scalable Gaussian Process framework.

problem: Deep graph neural networks suffer from oversmoothing where node features converge to homogeneous non-informative states, limiting representational capacity.
approach: Reframes oversmoothing via bifurcation theory, proving that replacing monotone activations with a specific class of functions breaks stability of homogeneous fixed points and creates stable non-homogeneous patterns.
contribution: Analytically proves activation substitution induces bifurcation with precise scaling laws for emergent patterns, and derives closed-form bifurcation-aware initialization improving real benchmarks.

problem: Heterogeneous multi-modal remote sensing detection suffers from entangled modality alignment and task-specific optimization during downstream learning, causing unstable training and poor generalization.
approach: BabelRS decouples modality alignment from task learning via language pivoting, using Concept-Shared Instruction Aligning to map sensor modalities to linguistic concepts and Layerwise Visual-Semantic Annealing for granularity matching.
contribution: Stabilizes training and consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods on heterogeneous multi-modal detection without additional bells and whistles.

problem: Existing reinforcement learning methods for reasoning focus on single-domain tasks with verifiable rewards and restrict exploration space, limiting multi-domain reasoning performance.
approach: RGR-GRPO leverages rubrics to provide dense fine-grained rewards and offline guidance, enabling larger solution space exploration during GRPO training across multiple domains.
contribution: Achieves average improvements of +7.0%, +5.4%, +8.4%, and +6.6% on mathematics, physics, chemistry, and general reasoning tasks with sustained exploration and superior pass@k performance.

problem: Medical vision-language pretraining with limited paired data struggles with global alignment dominated by non-diagnostic information and local alignment failing to integrate diagnostic evidence.
approach: LGDEA leverages LLMs to extract diagnostic evidence from reports and constructs shared diagnostic evidence spaces, enabling evidence-aware cross-modal alignment and effective use of unpaired data.
contribution: Achieves consistent and significant improvements on phrase grounding, image-text retrieval, and zero-shot classification while rivaling methods relying on substantial paired data.

problem: Memory-intensive AdamW optimizer limits practical LLM training on resource-constrained devices despite critical need for efficient alternatives.
approach: BAS bridges Adam and SignSGD via block-wise scaling of sign updates, reducing memory to 12.5% of AdamW by discarding element-wise second moments and storing first moment in FP8.
contribution: Achieves AdamW-equivalent performance without hyperparameter re-tuning across extensive evaluations including 1.5B pretraining and 32B fine-tuning, with communication-efficient variant.

problem: Transformers often fail to learn generalizable algorithms, instead relying on brittle heuristics that don't generalize beyond training distribution.
approach: Analyzes a simplified Disentangled Transformer architecture, proving it can compute graph connectivity via powers of adjacency matrix, and shows algorithm learning depends on whether most training instances fit model capacity.
contribution: Proves transformers learn algorithms when within-capacity graphs dominate training, and demonstrates transferability to standard transformers by restricting data to model capacity.

problem: Fairness-aware graph adaptation typically requires target-domain attributes for learning invariant representations, but such attributes are often unavailable in practice.
approach: CELL constructs causal graphs modeling generation mechanisms, uses sensitive and causal encoders with disentanglement via conditional mutual information, generates pseudo-labels, and builds fairness-aware bipartite graphs for structural supervision.
contribution: Consistently outperforms strong baselines in predictive performance and fairness on benchmarks without requiring target sensitive labels through causality-attended representation disentanglement.

problem: Spiking neural networks lag behind artificial neural networks in 3D understanding due to weak pretraining and heavy inference stacks, limiting generalization and multimodal reasoning.
approach: SVL proposes spike-based vision-language pretraining with Multi-scale Triple Alignment and Re-parameterizable Vision-Language Integration, plus first fully spike-driven PointFormer with 3D spike-driven self-attention.
contribution: Achieves 85.4% zero-shot 3D classification and outperforms SNNs on diverse tasks (+6.1% 3D cls, +2.1% DVS actions) while enabling energy-efficient open-world understanding sometimes surpassing ANNs.

problem: Group-based optimization for generative models suffers from rapid intra-group variance decay, eliminating learning signals and causing premature stagnation or reward hacking.
approach: E2PO sustains optimization through embedding-level perturbations within sample groups, introducing structured perturbations that guarantee robust discriminative variance throughout training.
contribution: Significantly outperforms state-of-the-art baselines achieving more faithful alignment with human preference through preservation of variance in training.

problem: Search agent benchmarks assume complete unambiguous queries, leaving under-tested practical failure: agents lack interactive mechanisms to resolve ambiguous requests during search.
approach: InteractComp benchmarks 210 expert-curated questions with controlled ambiguity, evaluating if agents recognize ambiguity and actively interact to resolve it during search.
contribution: Reveals striking failure with best model achieving only 13.73% despite 71.50% with complete context, with forced interaction producing dramatic gains and demonstrating latent capability.

problem: Multimodal agents struggle with inefficient tool use and inflexible orchestration in open-ended settings, unable to continually improve from past trajectories without parameter updates.
approach: XSkill proposes dual-stream framework extracting reusable experiences (action-level guidance) and skills (task-level guidance) grounded in visual observations, with visual-context-aware retrieval and continual learning loop.
contribution: Consistently and substantially outperforms tool-only and learning baselines across five benchmarks, with complementary knowledge streams showing superior zero-shot generalization.

problem: Current theory on feature learning strength in neural networks offers limited insight into generalization under practical training conditions like early stopping.
approach: Analyzes feature learning strength effects through empirical studies and gradient flow dynamics in two-layer ReLU networks, revealing optimal FLS arising from trade-off between over-alignment and over-fitting.
contribution: Establishes existence of optimal feature learning strength counter to prevailing intuition, showing large FLS induces over-alignment degrading generalization while small FLS leads to over-fitting.

problem: Novel view synthesis models struggle with semantically implausible and distorted images under long-range camera motion due to insufficient scene understanding.
approach: SemanticNVS integrates pre-trained semantic feature extractors into camera-conditioned multi-view diffusion models, using warped semantic features and alternating understanding-generation cycles.
contribution: Achieves 4.69%-15.26% improvement in FID over state-of-the-art alternatives through strong scene semantic conditioning enabling high-quality generation at distant viewpoints.

problem: Existing certified defenses struggle to simultaneously achieve provable robustness under l2 certificates and empirical robustness against strong l-infinity attacks.
approach: HySCAN introduces hybrid randomized defense combining stochastic weight-space randomness via Random Weights and explicit feature-space randomness via Stochastic Attention Noise Injection.
contribution: Improves certified robustness by up to 9.6% and empirical robustness by up to 5% without reducing clean accuracy across diverse imaging datasets.

problem: GUI agents depend on static parametric knowledge from pretraining, limiting ability to handle long-tailed tasks requiring explicit procedural knowledge absent from model parameters.
approach: DocOS proposes paradigm enabling agents to autonomously search for relevant documentation in dynamic web environments, and provides benchmark assessing document-guided problem solving in interactive settings.
contribution: Reveals dual bottlenecks: agents struggle to locate relevant information during proactive search and fail to ground retrieved instructions into precise GUI actions in interactive environments.

problem: Asynchronous stochastic gradient descent with constant step sizes suffers from degraded convergence due to large delays from slow workers.
approach: Provides theoretical justification for empirical observation that gradient clipping stabilizes asynchronous training, employing sub-Weibull noise model generalizing sub-Gaussian and sub-exponential distributions.
contribution: Shows clipping removes dependence on maximum delay in oracle complexity, with convergence in expectation and high-probability convergence guarantees in asynchronous optimization.

problem: Post-training quantization of LLMs relies on conventional Min-Max formula for quantization parameter initialization, which is suboptimal and underexplored.
approach: NeUQI identifies Min-Max limitations and proposes near-optimal initialization by deriving zero-point for given scale, reducing scale-only optimization through joint scale-zero-point learning.
contribution: Consistently outperforms existing PTQ methods on LLaMA and Qwen families, and achieves superior performance to PV-tuning when combined with lightweight distillation.

problem: Real-world depth sensing exhibits complex heterogeneous noise patterns deviating significantly from simulation, posing fundamental sim-to-real transfer bottleneck.
approach: PRISM introduces physics-grounded paradigm disentangling noise into sensing invalidation and measurement inaccuracy, using 3D Visual Foundation Model features with Hierarchical Positive-Prioritized Supervision.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art noisy depth synthesis fidelity and 92.1% average success rate in real-world robotic tasks, marking significant improvement over monolithic baselines.
